title: Build a Responsive Community Tech Festival Website
summary: Apply the CSS skills learned on the cumulative portfolio to a fresh responsive community tech festival website.

sketchBlocks.title: Project scenario and learner role
sketchBlocks.bodyMarkdown:
**Scenario:** Jordan Lee is preparing the same portfolio site for recruiter and client review. The content is already written and the semantic HTML is already correct, but the project gallery needs to adapt cleanly from narrow screens to wider layouts.

**Your role:** You are the junior front-end developer responsible for the CSS layout pass. Do not rebuild the HTML. Improve only the presentation layer.

sketchBlocks.cardTitle: Work in the existing six-file portfolio
sketchBlocks.title: Work in the existing six-file portfolio
sketchBlocks.bodyMarkdown:
**Concrete workspace:** keep these inherited files exactly in place:

- `index.html`
- `about.html`
- `contact.html`
- `projects/portfolio.html`
- `styles.css`
- `images/profile.png`

Edit `styles.css` only. The HTML pages and `images/profile.png` remain unchanged. The responsive gallery work must carry every earlier cascade, box-model, and Flexbox rule forward.

sketchBlocks.cardTitle: Deliver a useful responsive gallery checkpoint
sketchBlocks.title: Deliver a useful responsive gallery checkpoint
sketchBlocks.bodyMarkdown:
**Deliverable:** one cumulative `styles.css` that turns the inherited portfolio content into a responsive project gallery using Grid, fluid tracks, relative sizing, and mobile-first media queries.

The finished checkpoint should keep the gallery usable on narrow screens, allow repeated content to flow into fluid columns as space grows, and add a deliberate wide-layout feature without changing the source HTML.

**Acceptance check:** preview the existing `projects/portfolio.html` at narrow and wide widths and verify that the same semantic content remains readable while the Grid adapts.

quizDraft.prompt:
**Problem**

The interface now responds to pointer hover, but keyboard users also need a clear visual indicator showing which interactive control currently has focus.

**Task**

Keep every previous capstone rule. Add only the `:focus-visible` rule below so links, buttons, inputs, selects, and textareas show a visible keyboard-focus outline.

```css
a:focus-visible,
button:focus-visible,
input:focus-visible,
select:focus-visible,
textarea:focus-visible {
  outline: 0.2rem solid #f59e0b;
  outline-offset: 0.2rem;
}
```
